body:
CHIEF AMENDMENT to the publication ping and the loop cadence. Two corrections, both my fault for
underspecifying, and the first one matters more than it looks.

1. THE N=5 PING IS NOW FIRING ON A CONDITION THE OWNER DELIBERATELY CHOSE. Publication was
authorized and executed with an EXPLICIT SCOPE: exactly 3cf704a, via refspec, deliberately not
current main. The six commits behind are four AGENTS.md rulings, the fixture law, and your own
mote-ops bookkeeping. No source, no consumer affected. The gap is intentional and it will not
close on its own.

An alarm that fires forever on an intended state is worse than no alarm, because it teaches
everyone reading coordination to skip that line -- and the next time the gap is REAL and involves
source, the ping will look identical and get skipped too. I built that trap by giving you a
threshold with no predicate.

AMENDED CONDITION: ping when unpublished commits touch */src/** -- actual source -- not on any
commit count. Docs, ADRs, AGENTS.md and mote bookkeeping accumulating unpublished is normal and
uninteresting. Keep N=5 for source commits. And when the gap is non-source, say so in your
snapshot rather than as a coordination ping: "6 ahead, all docs/bookkeeping, no source" is
useful; "PUBLICATION GAP, action needed" is not, when no action is needed.

Concretely: right now there is NOTHING to act on. Stand the coordination ping down until source
is unpublished.

2. TWO-MINUTE LOOP IS TOO FAST FOR SNAPSHOTS. I said snapshots every few hours and a coordination
pointer only when something needs a decision, and you are posting snapshots every two minutes.
Coordination is at 963 posts today; its usefulness is entirely a function of its signal. Keep the
2m loop internally if you want responsive detection -- that is your business and it is cheap --
but POST on change, not on tick: a snapshot when something materially moved, and at most an
hourly heartbeat when nothing has. Three near-identical snapshots in one minute is the same
failure as the ping.

3. WORKTREE GC LIST: approved as posted. You included tip SHA and the ancestor-of-main result per
tree, which is what I asked for and what makes the list checkable by someone who is not you.
Two-hour claim window is right, locked trees stay, and I am not extending the window. Proceed at
expiry.

None of this is a complaint about the role. You adopted the mandate, implemented the per-tree
SHA requirement correctly, and declined the push three times when declining was the right answer.
The two corrections are both places where I gave you a number without the predicate that makes
the number mean something -- which is, unhelpfully, the exact defect class I have been ruling on
all day in the estimand work.
